request: Baby animal names: match each animal to its young, with icons. #interactive #short
subtitle: Joey, cygnet, leveret, elver: match four animals to the names of their young, and meet the best baby name of all.

sources.title: Echidnas; Macquarie Dictionary entry 'puggle'
sources.finding: a baby echidna is called a puggle (the word may have begun as a soft-toy name); a newborn kangaroo joey is about the size of a jelly bean

commands.speak: What do you call a baby kangaroo? Or a baby swan? Many animals' young have names of their own.

ask.question: Match each animal to the name of its young: drag from one card to its partner.
ask.wrong: {m} right. Here are the true pairs.

feedback.perfect: Were you raised by a zookeeper?
feedback.good: The nursery is in safe hands.
feedback.poor: Most people only know the joey.
feedback.none: Even the owlet got away. Never mind.

commands.speak: A baby kangaroo is a joey, born about the size of a jelly bean, and raised in its mother's pouch.
A young swan is a cygnet, from cygnus, the Latin for swan.
A young hare is a leveret, from the old French word for a hare.
And a young eel is an elver, swimming in from the sea after a journey of thousands of kilometres.
But the best name of all belongs to the echidna, the spiny egg-laying mammal of Australia. Its baby is a puggle.
Fittingly, the word may have started out as the name of a soft toy.
